prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mechanics, electrical engineering, sensor technology, actuator technology, and control engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Learned methods for the development of complex mechatronic systems can be safely applied to problems.
Students can independently explore unknown subject areas based on the learned methods.
The acquired knowledge enables students to introduce methods into the professional world, based on solid scientific findings, upon which complex mechatronic systems can also be developed.
Students safely recognize and avoid outdated approaches.

syllabus_topics: Representation of the development process of a mechatronic system using the V-model of development
Creation of Use Cases for a mechatronic system
Collection of system requirements, creation of the system design
Requirement decomposition towards SW development, electronics development, mechanics development
Creation of Test Cases at system and component level
Completing requirements for a mechatronic system, dealing with stakeholders
Design of a system architecture for an exemplary mechatronic system
Requirement decomposition and accompanying its implementation
assessment_rules: The graded part of the examination is an oral project report on the system developed in the internship and the non-instructor-led part, including reference to the theoretical part of the course. This will involve an results presentation of 25-30 minutes, followed by a discussion of the same duration. The presentation should have a scope of 15-30 slides. Regular participation in the internship is required, meaning at least 80% attendance.
bibliography: Heimann, B.; u. a.: „Mechatronik: Eine Einführung in die Komponenten zur Synthese und die Methoden zur Analyse mechatronischer Systeme“, Hanser-Verlag, 2015
